verdicts.conditionQuote: Today they run in an in-process worker pool, so a deploy or a crash loses any job that was queued but not yet started.
verdicts.note: Context and motivation (the current problem), not a limit on any claim.

verdicts.conditionQuote: Uses spare capacity on the existing primary
verdicts.note: The u15 note qualifies '$0 extra' as relying on spare primary capacity (tied to u34's month-end risk); the u14 row is plain cost data.

verdicts.conditionQuote: The managed queue's figure assumes current volume. At three times today's volume it would be roughly $900 a month
verdicts.note: The $310 figure is misleading at the 3x volume the must-have criteria plan for.

verdicts.conditionQuote: an option that fails either is out regardless of its score
verdicts.claimQuote: The remaining criteria are weighted for scoring
verdicts.note: Reading 1 (claim): weighted scores/rankings mislead without the gate that disqualifies regardless of score; reading 2 (set): the weighting statement stays true and the gate is a separate decision rule.

verdicts.conditionQuote: Portability away from our cloud provider: 10%
verdicts.note: A criterion weight, not a limit on a claim.

verdicts.conditionQuote: every job handler must be made idempotent before we switch; today only the email handler is
verdicts.claimQuote: Option A needs almost no operational work
verdicts.note: At-least-once delivery makes Option A unsafe until handlers are idempotent; 'almost no work' read alone misleads about adopting it.

verdicts.conditionQuote: It also ties us to one provider's API, and local development needs an emulator that does not support dead-lettering.
verdicts.claimQuote: failed messages move to a dead-letter queue automatically
verdicts.note: Lock-in and a local-dev gap in dead-lettering; the production claim stays true.

verdicts.conditionQuote: the 12 hours a month is an estimate, not a measurement
verdicts.note: Epistemic caveat on the effort figure, which is already hedged with 'about'.

verdicts.claimQuote: A message broker cluster of three virtual machines that we install, patch and monitor ourselves.
verdicts.note: An operational cost of Option B; could be judged too minor.

verdicts.conditionQuote: That guarantee only covers jobs created inside the billing database transaction; jobs enqueued by the reporting service, which has its own database, would not get it.
verdicts.claimQuote: a job can never be lost between the commit and the enqueue
verdicts.note: 'Never be lost' is false for reporting-service jobs.

verdicts.conditionQuote: Polling also adds read load to the primary database, which is the main risk at month-end.
verdicts.claimQuote: Database job table | $0 extra | about 4 hours | Uses spare capacity on the existing primary
verdicts.note: Main risk of Option C; the cost row stays true.

verdicts.conditionQuote: It sustained 1,200 jobs per minute with a p95 claim latency of 18 ms.
verdicts.note: A measured result (a claim), which u38 limits, not itself a condition.

verdicts.conditionQuote: We did not test 1,800 jobs per minute, and the staging copy is about a quarter of production size, so these results may not carry over.
verdicts.claimQuote: It sustained 1,200 jobs per minute with a p95 claim latency of 18 ms.
verdicts.note: Without this, the load-test result reads as evidence Option C meets production needs.

verdicts.conditionQuote: We have not load-tested Options A or B. ... but that is the provider's figure, not ours.
verdicts.claimQuote: The provider documents throughput far above our peak for Option A
verdicts.note: Evidence gap for A and B; the documented-throughput claim stays true as attributed.

verdicts.conditionQuote: The decision is deferred until Option C has been measured at 1,800 jobs per minute on a production-sized database.
